title: The Day a Bank Teller's Bluff Beat the James Gang
mechanism: A time lock is a clockwork in a safe door that keeps the bolts from moving until the hour it is set to; Heywood's had never been set, so the safe was unlocked, but the outlaws believed his bluff and never tried the handle while the town armed itself outside.

beats.hook: He told eight armed outlaws the bank safe was locked. It wasn't: the camera glides through a dark vault onto an iron safe with a little TIME LOCK window and an outlaw's revolver.
beats.but: The James-Younger gang rides into quiet Northfield; inside the bank sits acting cashier Joseph Heywood.
beats.then: An outlaw orders him to open the safe; Heywood says it's on a time lock; one outlaw steps into the vault and Heywood throws the heavy door on him.
beats.conflict: Teller Bunker bolts out the back, shot in the shoulder; outside a hardware merchant grabs his rifle: 'Get your guns, boys!'
beats.pivot: You see, a time lock is a clock in the safe door: once set, nobody opens it until the hour comes. But Heywood's clock had never been set.
beats.so: Bullets fill the street; the gang flees with $26.70; three killed, three captured.
beats.closing: Heywood paid for his bluff with his life; the bookkeeper turns the handle and the safe swings open on the untouched money.

seed.what: The small TIME LOCK window on the safe door, its clock hands stopped, and the brass handle nobody tries
